BIGGEST STRUCTURAL FINDING. The crate calls itself the product runtime, but its only non-test consumer in the whole workspace is the benchmark: `grep -rn "client-core" --include=Cargo.toml crates/` returns exactly crates/bench/Cargo.toml:13. There is no binary, no hub-server or client binary depending on it. So "product path" today means "the path bench drives". Everything classified SHIP is SHIP-shaped and exercised, but it is exercised by crates/bench/src/kama_product.rs, crates/client-core/tests/runtime_e2e.rs and two examples — not by a shipping application.

SECOND STRUCTURAL FINDING. The runtime is UNIDIRECTIONAL. server_task holds no adaptive_transport::Sender (verified: every `Sender` hit in the server half is a tokio channel type). Return-direction frames — ACK, RECOVERED, PARAM_ACK, CS echo — are written straight to the socket through srv_seal_send (runtime.rs:1842) with no pacing, no congestion control, no ARQ, no loss ledger and no retry. Any claim of the form "Kama transport beats X" currently covers one direction of data only.

THIRD. Every measurement to date ran with IdentitySeam (seam.rs:111): a +16 B zero tag with no confidentiality, no integrity, no per-peer identity (open always returns peer 0, seam.rs:135). The seam boundary looks S2-ready (fallible seal, SealArgs/meta, sealed_len contract) but four SealError variants and three OpenReject variants have zero constructors anywhere, and SealedDatagram.full_wire_pn/dh_epoch are written by every impl and read by none — the §0.5 send-record return path is open at this seam.

COUNTER HYGIENE. Five ClientStats fields and six [C4-ATIF] ServerStats attribution counters are incremented on the hot path and read by nothing but `_`-bindings in the API-surface pin test; FateWindowDiag.rtt_samples has zero readers of any kind; FateWindowDiag.sched is a 12-element array that is all zeros in the default build because diag-sched-telemetry is OFF (crates/adaptive-transport/src/sender.rs:4370). That last one is the vacuous-counter shape: it reports zeros rather than being absent, so a reader cannot tell "no denials" from "telemetry not compiled" without checking the feature flag.

DOC-vs-CODE CONTRADICTION worth a one-line fix (adaptive-transport, adjacent to scope): StartupPacingConfig's field doc (sender.rs:1075 "Default false -> inert") and set_startup_pacing_init's doc (sender.rs:2018 "default OFF") both contradict the actual value, sender.rs:1125 `Self { enabled: true }`. client-core never calls the setter, so the product rides that ON default; crates/client-core/src/lib.rs:70-72 states the correct value and even records that an earlier edit got it wrong.

BOUNDS NOTE (low severity, not filed as an item). `unit_seqs.entry(d.unit_id).or_default().push(d.seq)` (runtime.rs:1031) has no per-unit cap in client-core; it is bounded only indirectly by the engine's arq_retx_cap = 3 (crates/adaptive-transport/src/arq.rs:73) and TailRecoveryConfig::max_tail_probes. If either engine bound moves, this Vec grows without a client-core-side limit, which is the shape SR-AUDIT-001 forbids.

METHOD. Every classification was decided by grepping the symbol across crates/ and labelling each call site product / bench / test / example, then reading the gating expression. No classification was inferred from a name or comment; where a comment and the code disagreed (startup pacing, lib.rs:77 FEC default) the code was taken as authoritative and the disagreement reported.
